title: Inspiration Behind Braiding Sweetgrass
text: Inspiration Behind Braiding Sweetgrass R obin Wall Kimmerer is a Native American woman and a member of the Citizen Potawatomi Nation. She is a professor of Environmental and Forest Biology at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry (SUNY-ESF) , Kimmerer makes an effort to combine her scientific passion for plants, forests, and biology with her native Potawatomi heritage and knowledge. She has written two books, Gathering Moss: A Natural and Cultural History of Mosses , and this book, Braiding Sweetgrass: Indigenous Wisdom, Scientific Knowledge and the Teachings of Plants , both on the subject of how Native American knowledge about plants can help scientific study by acknowledging relationships between different living beings. Braiding Sweetgrass: Indigenous Wisdom, Scientific Knowledge and the Teachings of Plants was published on the 15 th of October 2013 by Milkweed Editions. The hardcover edition of the book has 391 pages. A special hardcover edition was published with a new introduction from Robin Wall Kimmerer in honor of the fortieth anniversary of Milkweed Editions, a nonprofit publishing company. The book was reissued as an object of meaning that will last for a long time. The cover is designed by Tony Drehfal and contains an engraving as well as a deckled edge and a bookmark ribbon. The new edition also contains five colorful illustrations by artist Nate Christopherson. The book quickly became a hit and appeared on the bestseller lists of The New York Times , The Washington Post , and Los Angeles Times . Literary Hub also gave the book the epithet of “Best Essay Collection of the Decade”, while The Washington Post and Minneapolis Star Tribune also put it on their lists for holiday gift recommendations. Book Riot and Food Tank also highly recommended it. Braiding Sweetgrass won the 2014 Sigurd F. Olson Nature Writing Award, given in honor of the literary legacy of Sigurd F. Olson to the best environmental writings in adult nonfiction and children’s literature. Despite its success, Braiding Sweetgrass did not have a large-scale marketing campaign. Instead, it became popular through “word of mouth” and recommendations from one reader to the other. According to the author, this may be because the time is ripe for the message when inequalities and injustices have become so apparent. Kimmerer wrote the first draft of the book in purple ink on long yellow legal pads, sitting outside in nature and observing small things in the natural world that can act as microcosms for great ideas. The name, Braiding Sweetgrass , is a metaphor referring to the fact that the stories told in the book are made up of three strands: the traditional indigenous perspective about environment, scientific knowledge about plants, and the beauty of the knowledge that plants themselves hold and can teach those who want to learn. The book is supposed to be a braid of stories using three different ways of defining our relationship with the natural world. Braiding Sweetgrass has a rating of 4.58 on Goodreads and 4.8 on Amazon. The book has been praised for being a profoundly important work. The few criticisms of the book state that the stories run together and are often repetitive, and the author’s presentation of the subject is completely one-sided, not taking into account the social problems of indigenous or traditional societies. However, the book remains popular, and the author has been commended on her take on this complicated subject.
